content.text: File permission mode: Read Only: no automatic file writes. Shell enforces the file policy; apply_patch rejects disallowed paths. Use shell sandbox_permissions: require_escalated to request one-time approval when broader file access is needed. run_code and plugin tools require one-time approval because their execution is not file-sandboxed. Network access is unchanged.

tools.name: wait
tools.description: [parallel_safe] Tools, including run_code programs, automatically return task_id when they are queued or exceed their yield time; no separate background mode is required. wait returns when the task completes or yield_time_ms expires, with output produced since the previous receipt. Expiry does not stop the task; its execution deadline remains separate. Program-side await tools.* waits for the actual result. terminate requests cancellation; receipts report queued/running state, confirmable or best_effort cancellation, and resource_scope without exposing resource keys. Running claims/bundle/runtime resources stay busy; independent tasks can coexist. Only cancelled/timed_out confirm cancellation. Tasks belong to this Host instance and do not resume after restart. Local shell receipts may include independent foreground/stdio observations; foreground_exit_code is available after the direct process exits, even while status is running. Only running + foreground=exited + stdio=open derives foreground_exited, a nonterminal label. EOF alone is not completion; forced pipe closure is not observed EOF. terminate/timeout follows the originating Shell runtime's declared ownership scope (POSIX process group; Windows direct child unless the Host declares an identity-verified adapter). Escaped descendants may survive, and unconfirmed cleanup remains explicitly unconfirmed.
